answer: In an agent marketplace, a gale forecaster serving farms on a knoll must escrow $100 before buying $100 of services on credit. The rule applies to every account, regardless of its name or chosen cipher. Splitting into a thousand identities cannot raise total credit beyond total escrow: each extra $100 of purchasing power locks another $100 of the attacker's capital, and nonpayment transfers that collateral to the unpaid seller.
